title: Getting around, making plans
cando: buy a ticket, make a plan with someone and give reasons

about.text: This is the last lesson of Level 1. You buy a train ticket and plan a day by the sea. You also read a departures board and give reasons for your plans.
goals: Buy a ticket: A return to Sandmouth, please.
Ask about a train: What time does it leave? Which platform?
Ask and offer: Can I have a window seat? I'll wait for you.
Give reasons: because work is busy, to buy coffee.
Read a departures board and a ticket, and text a friend a plan.

chapters.title: At the ticket desk
chapters.text:
This is the last lesson of Level 1. You travel by train, and you make plans.
First, you listen to Tomasz at the ticket desk. He wants to go to the sea tomorrow.
The clerk asks: Single or return? A single takes you there. A return takes you there and back.
Tomasz asks: What time does the first train leave? Listen for the time and the platform.
Then he meets his colleague Ana. She asks: Shall we go together? That is an idea for two people.

chapters.title: Offers and reasons
chapters.text:
To ask for something, say Can I…? Can I have a window seat, please?
To offer to do something, say I'll and a verb. I'll wait for you. I'll buy the tickets.
I'll is I will. Say it as one short word.
To give a reason, use because and a sentence. I need a day at the beach because work is busy.
Or use to and a verb. I'll come early to buy coffee. After to, the verb does not change.

chapters.title: A departures board
chapters.text:
Next, you read a departures board at a station.
It shows the time, the place and the platform of each train.
Look at the end of each line. Is the train on time, delayed or cancelled?
Then you read a ticket. Find the date, the seat and the last train back.
Last, you write a text to a friend with a plan. Give one or two reasons.

chapters.title: Planning a day trip
chapters.text:
In the task, you plan a day trip with a friend. First, you choose a train together, and you say why.
Then you buy two tickets at the desk. Ask about the time and the platform.
Then you send your friend a text with the plan. Say the train, the platform and where to meet.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story about a day out.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again and answer the questions.
After this lesson comes the A1 review and check. Then you start Level 2.

warmup.prompt: You want a day out by the sea. How do you like to travel?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. The train is often quicker. A car or a bus can be cheaper for a group.

conversation.title: At the ticket desk
conversation.setting: It is Friday afternoon. Tomasz is at the ticket desk at Hillford station. He wants a day by the sea tomorrow. His colleague Ana is in the queue behind him.
lines: Good afternoon. Can I help you?
Yes, please. A ticket to Sandmouth for tomorrow, please.
A return, please. What time does the first train leave?
At 8:15, from platform 2. It arrives at 9:40.
8:15, platform 2. Can I have a window seat, please?
Tomasz! Hi! Are you going to Sandmouth tomorrow? Me too!
Hi, Ana! Yes. I need a day at the beach because work is so busy.
I know! Shall we go together?
Sure, good idea! I'll wait for you on platform 2 at eight.
Great. I'll come early to buy coffee for us.
Good plan. And maybe we can have lunch by the sea.
Yes! I'll send you a text tonight. See you tomorrow!

a return to Sandmouth for today

items.meaning: A paper or card that shows you paid. You need it for a train, a bus or a film.
items.example: Can I have a ticket to Sandmouth, please?

items.meaning: A ticket to go to a place, but not to come back.

items.meaning: It carries a lot of people from station to station.
items.example: I go to work by train.

items.meaning: The place in a station where you wait and get on the train.
items.example: The train leaves from platform 2.

items.meaning: A place to sit, on a train, a bus or in a cinema.
items.example: Excuse me, is this seat free?

items.meaning: To go away from a place. The past is left.
items.example: The train leaves at 8:15.

items.meaning: To get to the place you are going to.
items.example: The train arrives in Sandmouth at 9:40.

items.meaning: On this day.

items.meaning: On the day after today.

items.meaning: A friendly yes.

items.meaning: Not yes and not no. It can happen, or not.

sound.title: I'll: will as one short word
sound.explain: People often say I will as one short word: I'll. We'll and you'll are the same. Say each one as one sound. Listen, then say each group.
lines: I'll wait for you on platform 2.
I'll send you a text tonight.

sayIt.instructions: Say Tomasz's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Do you say I'll as one short word?
lines: Yes, please. A ticket to Sandmouth for tomorrow, please.
A return, please. What time does the first train leave?
8:15, platform 2. Can I have a window seat, please?
Sure, good idea! I'll wait for you on platform 2 at eight.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. One asks for something. One offers to do something. Two give a reason.
examples: Can I have a window seat, please?
I'll wait for you on platform 2 at eight.
I need a day at the beach because work is so busy.
I'll come early to buy coffee for us.
spot.question: Which sentence asks for something? Which one offers? Which two give a reason, and how?
spot.answer: Can I have …? asks for something. I'll wait for you is an offer: I'll + a verb. Because work is so busy gives a reason. To buy coffee gives a reason too: to + a verb.

rules.title: Asking and offering: Can I…? and I'll…
rule: Ask for something: Can I have a window seat? Can you help me, please?
Answer: Sure. / Of course. / Sorry, no.
Offer: I'll + a verb: I'll buy the tickets. I'll wait for you.
I'll = I will. After will, there is no to and no -s.
An idea for two people: Shall we go together? — Sure!
rules.mistake: Not: I'll to wait for you. Say: I'll wait for you.

rules.title: Giving a reason: because, and to + a verb
rule: because + a sentence: We're taking the train because it's quicker.
to + a verb also says why: I went there to buy a ticket.
Why are you going? — To see the sea. / Because I need a rest.
After to, the verb does not change: to buy, to see, to meet.
Write because in the same sentence: I stayed at home because it rained.
rules.mistake: Not: I went to the shop for buy bread. Say: I went to the shop to buy bread.

practice.q: ___ I have a window seat, please?
practice.why: Asking for something: Can I have …?

practice.q: My bag is very heavy. — I'll ___ it for you.
practice.why: I'll + a verb, with no to and no -s.

practice.q: I ___ send you a text tonight.
practice.why: will + a verb: I will send. No to.

practice.q: ___ we go to the beach together? — Sure, good idea!
practice.why: Shall we …? gives an idea for two people.

practice.q: We're taking the train ___ it's quicker than the bus.
practice.why: Because + a sentence gives the reason.

practice.q: I went to the airport ___ meet my sister. Her plane was late.
practice.why: To + a verb says why: to meet.

practice.q: I'm learning English ___ I want a better job.
practice.why: Because + a sentence: because I want a better job.

practice.q: I'm learning English to ___ a better job.
practice.why: After to, the verb does not change: to get.

practice.q: ___ you help me with my bag, please? — Sure.
practice.why: Can you …? asks a person to do something.

practice.q: Can I sit here? — ___ . It's my friend's seat.
practice.why: The seat is for a friend, so the answer is no.

yourTurn.prompt: Why are you learning English? Write three reasons. Use because in one sentence, and to + a verb in two.
yourTurn.model: I'm learning English because I want a better job. I'm learning it to talk to my colleagues. I also need English to help my family at the doctor's.

text.title: Departures, and a ticket
text.body:
HILLFORD STATION · DEPARTURES
Saturday 13 June · 08:05

08:10 · Kellbridge · Platform 1 · On time
08:15 · Sandmouth · Platform 2 · Delayed: now 08:40
08:30 · Kellbridge · Platform 1 · Cancelled
08:45 · Sandmouth · Platform 2 · On time
09:00 · Kellbridge Airport · Platform 3 · On time

We are sorry for the delay to the 08:15.
Platform 2: cross the bridge. Allow 4 minutes.
Going to the airport? Take the 09:00.
Sandmouth: sun, sea and boat trips from the beach!

- - - - - - - -

PRACTICE TICKET: not valid for travel.
DAY RETURN · 1 ADULT
From: Hillford
To: Sandmouth
Date: 13 June
Out: 08:15 · Seat 24
Back: any train today (last departure 22:30)
Not valid on buses.
Price: £18.50

How do you get to platform 2?

detail.q: When is the last train back to Hillford?
detail.why: The ticket says: Back: any train today (last departure 22:30).

model.title: A text with a plan
model.body:
Hi Ana! Bad news: the 8:15 is delayed. It leaves at 8:40 now.
Shall we meet at 8:20, not 8:00? I'll wait on platform 2.
In Sandmouth, first the beach, because it's sunny in the morning.
At 2:00, we can take a boat to see the town.
We'll be back at about 7 tonight.
Tomasz

write.task: You and a friend are going on a day trip. Write your friend a text with the plan. Say the train, and where and when to meet. Give two reasons, with because or to.
write.starter: Hi …! Here's the plan for Saturday.
checklist: I said the train time and where to meet.
I made an offer with I'll.
I gave two reasons, with because or to + a verb.
I wrote my name at the end.

card.title: A day trip
card.situation: You and your friend Kwame want a day by the sea on Saturday. Look at the departures board in Section 3. You need two return tickets.
card.goal: Choose a train with Kwame, and say why. Buy two tickets at the desk. Then send Kwame a text with the plan.

phrases: The 8:15 is often late. Shall we get the 8:45?
What time does it leave, and which platform?
Can we have two seats together, please?
I'll buy the tickets. You can get the coffee.
The train is better because it's quicker than the car.
prepare.notes: Make notes: which train, and why. Where do you meet? What can you do there? Then write your text.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher is Kwame first. Choose a train together and give reasons. Then your teacher is the clerk: buy two tickets. Last, read your text to the class.
doIt.wehel: Let's plan a day trip to the sea. First, you are my friend Kwame. We choose a train together, and I give reasons. Then you are the clerk at the ticket desk, and I buy two return tickets. Use simple English.

model.title: Planning and buying the tickets
lines: Hi! So, which train shall we get on Saturday?
Yes, the 8:45 is good because it's always on time.
Great. Can you buy the tickets? I'll pay you back.
Sure. I'll buy them today, after work.
Two returns to Sandmouth for Saturday, please. On the 8:45.
Sure. That's £37, please. Would you like seats together?
Yes, please. Which platform does it leave from?

compare: Did you choose a train and give a reason with because?
Did you ask for two returns, and say the day and the train?
Did you make an offer with I'll?
Did your text say the time, the platform and where to meet?

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. Where are the people going? How are they travelling?
reading.talk: Was the trip in the story a good plan? Where would you like to go for a day trip, and why? Write two or three sentences with because, or say them to Wehel.

quiz.q: Single or return? — A ___ , please. I'm coming back tonight.
quiz.why: You are coming back, so you need a return.
What time does it leave? The train is it, so does.

quiz.q: It's cold in here. — I'll ___ the window.
quiz.why: An offer: I'll + a verb, with no to.

quiz.q: Why did you go to the bank? — ___ get some money.
quiz.why: To + a verb answers Why?: To get some money.

quiz.q: Your friend says: Shall we go to the beach? You want to say yes. What do you say?
quiz.why: Sure, good idea! is a friendly yes.

quiz.q: The board says: 10:15 Kellbridge · Delayed: now 10:35. How late is the train?
You wait for the train on the ___ .
quiz.why: The platform is where you get on the train.

quiz.q: This is the ___ café in town. The coffee is great!
quiz.why: The best: better than all the others.
Turn left at the traffic lights: at the place where you turn.

quiz.q: ___ you go out last weekend? — Yes, I went to a party.
quiz.why: A question about the past: Did you …?

liveClass: Day 1: ticket desk role-play in pairs. Change the place, the day and the ticket: a single, a return, two adults.
Day 2: an offer chain. One learner says a problem (My bag is heavy.), and the next makes an offer with I'll. Then each learner says why they are learning English, with because or to.
Day 3: the task. Pairs plan a day trip and choose a train. Then they buy two tickets from you at the desk, and read their text plan aloud.
Day 4: talk about the book and answer questions. Then look back at Level 1: each learner says three things they can do now in English.
